To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the bacterial healing agent, consisting of bacteria spores encapsulated in porous particles and a mineral precursor, calcium lactate, can be added to a concrete mix and that the bacterial agent can indeed be activated in a crack to produce a limestone based mineral which can subsequently seal and water-tight the crack.

(i) encapsulated bacteria can be used as a crack healing agent in concrete and (ii) that the bacteria can be encapsulated in porous aggregate material and can be used in a self-healing agent for concrete.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a self-healed concrete in which bacteria-based healing agents are used.
the development of a bacterial-based self-healing agent which can be used in the construction industry for the production of concrete with improved crack healing properties.
the development of an autonomous crack-healed concrete which features increased strength and prolonged service life.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bacterial-based self-healing concrete is an effective and efficient solution to improve the durability of cement based constructions.
the bacteria-based healing agent is capable of healing cracks of up to 0.15mm in width, and that this is an effective way to improve concrete durability.
the bacterial self-healing agent is capable of sealing cracks in concrete.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bacterial agent has the potential to improve durability and prolong service life of concrete structures by means of a self-healed crack mechanism.
we have developed a new type of concrete that can repair itself.
the bacteria-based concrete is able to self-heal damage in a similar manner as traditional concrete.

bacterial-based self-healing concrete is indeed possible and can be used to improve the durability of concrete constructions.
the bacterial-based agent is able to reduce permeability in cracked concrete specimens to a significant extent.
